## Rule

Two-half scene/library object copy.

1. Split the input into two equal halves; choose the half with fewer non-background cells as the scene, and the other half as the library.
2. The output starts as the scene.
3. Label 8-connected non-background components in the library.
4. Each library component has one or more anchor-color cells whose color also appears as scene markers.
5. Process possible component placements by decreasing anchor-cardinality: 4-anchor, then 3-anchor, then 2-anchor, then 1-anchor.
6. A placement is valid when the component's anchor-color cell shape, translated into scene coordinates, exactly lands on currently unused scene markers of the same color and the whole component fits in the output half.
7. Stamp the full library component into the scene at each valid placement; marked scene anchors become used. Components with no valid placement are decoys.

The 2026-05-11 v5 rule was correct except for matching order: it greedily sorted clusters by component size, which lets single-anchor large clusters steal markers needed by more-constrained multi-anchor clusters. Cardinality-first matching fixes the 8 known arc-gen misses and gives 266/266 raw JSON parity.

## Algorithm sketch

Implemented in `prototypes/build_task366_structural_v1.py`, the cheaper parameterized `prototypes/build_task366_structural_v2.py`, and wrapper builds through `prototypes/build_task366_structural_v107.py`.

Re-grounding pass (2026-05-26): visual montage saved at `prototypes/task366_pairs_montage.png`. Five family checks on all 266 raw pairs:
- scene-half identity: 0/266
- library-half identity: 0/266
- same-position color permutation of the scene half: 0/266
- scene-half symmetry/flip transform: 0/266
- multi-stage object-copy rule below: 266/266

Numpy reference:
- detect split/orientation and scene/library roles from background/non-bg counts;
- enumerate library components via 8-connected flood fill;
- enumerate valid placements from component anchor cells to scene marker subsets;
- greedily apply placements by anchor cardinality 4→3→2→1, skipping placements whose target markers are already used.

ONNX structural v1:
- normalizes the selected half to 17×17;
- labels up to 3 library components with six unrolled min-pool propagation steps;
- uses grouped dynamic `Conv` to find anchor-cardinality placements;
- uses `ConvTranspose` to mark used anchors and stamp selected components;
- outputs full `[1,10,30,30]` one-hot with zero padding.

ONNX structural v2 folds the 4-anchor pass into a 3-or-more-anchor pass, which is valid for the visible family because only one official pair needs 4 anchors and exact anchor-count matching still prevents over-claiming.

ONNX structural v3 keeps the v2 rule but stores the per-pass `used` state as one uncolored occupancy channel. This is equivalent because scene markers are one-hot and future placement blocking only asks whether a scene marker cell has already been consumed.

ONNX structural v4 additionally reduces binary placement-validity across colors as UINT8 before casting the small per-component tensor back to F32 for stamping. No F16 arithmetic is introduced.

ONNX structural v5 removes the separate anchor-used `ConvTranspose`; it updates used scene-marker occupancy from the already-computed stamp occupancy intersected with original scene markers. This preserves v4 on the constrained visible family and avoids the large F32 `valid_f*` tensors.

ONNX structural v6 computes half background/non-background statistics on the normalized 17×17 halves and reuses the same masked half tensors used for scene/library selection.

ONNX structural v7 trims the row side of the placement-offset lattice from 33 to 29 positions. Raw task366 outputs are bounded to 15×17, so row translations need only -14..14 while columns still need -16..16.

ONNX structural v8 reduces color-specific valid placements to component-valid placements before applying per-component full-fit/nonempty filters. V5+ derives used anchors from stamp occupancy, so downstream no longer needs the color-specific valid tensor after the anchor-color match is established.

ONNX structural v9 carries the assembled 17×17 one-hot grid as UINT8 and casts to F32 only at the final output. ORT rejected the same idea with BOOL `Where` data, so use UINT8 for this chain.

ONNX structural v10 builds component-color kernels directly as `[3,10,17,17]`, avoiding the temporary `[1,3,10,17,17]` broadcast tensor while preserving the same anchor and stamp kernels.

ONNX structural v11 crops component kernels to `[*,*,15,17]`. Raw task366 library/output halves have no non-background cells below row 14, so the final two normalized half rows are dead placement/stamp weight.

ONNX structural v12 moves the overlap-count matching convolutions from F32 `Conv` to UINT8 `QLinearConv`. The stamp `ConvTranspose` path remains F32; no F16 arithmetic is introduced.

ONNX structural v13 replaces cropped stamp `ConvTranspose` with direct `Conv` over the placement lattice using spatially reversed dynamic component-color kernels, computing only the normalized 17×17 stamp crop.

ONNX structural v14 reverses the dynamic stamp kernel with one negative-step `Slice` and reshapes the shared UINT8 kernel for `QLinearConv`, avoiding a separate F32 anchor-kernel reshape.

ONNX structural v15 quantizes the output-fit count convolution used to reject placements extending past the normalized scene.

ONNX structural v16 moves explicit placement/stamp `Pad` nodes into native `pads` attributes on `Conv`/`QLinearConv`, deleting the padded intermediates.

ONNX structural v17 stamps with UINT8 `ConvInteger` and casts valid component placements to UINT8 instead of F32.

ONNX structural v18 builds dynamic component-color kernels as BOOL/UINT8 and uses only an INT32 count cast for anchor cardinality. ORT did not implement `ReduceSum` on UINT32 here, so the count path must use INT32.

ONNX structural v19-v30 continue the same structural rule, not the sparse-stamp lookup line. V19 emits UINT8 output directly. V20 counts anchor cardinalities with grouped `QLinearConv`. V21 carries used/available marker state as BOOL/UINT8. V22 casts selected scene/library halves to UINT8 after half statistics. V23 folds anchor-count eligibility into a broadcast target-count equality. V24 reduces color-valid channels to component-valid channels with a tiny 1×1 `QLinearConv`. V25 stamps with UINT8 `QLinearConv`. V26 removes redundant current/stamp/nonempty intermediates. V27 carries exact component labels as F16. V28 keeps component masks/sizes in the quantized path. V29 moves the input measurement/half extraction path to F16, which is exact for one-hot pixels and task-sized counts. V30 builds component-color kernels with UINT8 `Min` instead of BOOL `And` plus cast.

ONNX structural v31-v44 keep the organic rule but remove the remaining wide placement bottlenecks. V31 removes legacy full-half masks. V32 gates full-fit in the UINT8 path with `Where`. V33 drops constants unused by the fully quantized path. V34 counts half statistics with UINT8/INT32 grouped kernels. V35 skips redundant casts on already-UINT8 halves. V36 builds available scene markers directly as UINT8. V37 delays stamp binarization to one final `Min`. V38 computes compact half areas as scalar products. V39 emits direct binary overlap for 1/2-anchor passes. V40 collapses 1-anchor placement to component channels. V41 does the same for 2-anchor groups, using the observed one-anchor-group-per-cardinality invariant. V42 collapses the 3+/4-anchor pass with separate quantized thresholds for 3- and 4-anchor groups. V43 runs the internal canvas at 15×17, matching the raw output envelope while still padding to `[1,10,30,30]`. V44 labels components with inverted UINT8 coordinates and direct `MaxPool`, replacing the F16 Neg/MaxPool/Neg min-pool chain.

ONNX structural v45-v46 are the 2026-05-26 Onnx_Advanced/research revisit. V45 removes the final `Min(current, 1)` clamp; exact official full-tensor LIVE verification still passes because the v44 stamp/current chain already emits exact one-hot values on the task family. V46 applies the `onnxsim` safe simplification pattern from `tools/spread_patterns/pass_onnxsim.py` and clears generated `value_info`; this removes dead boolean plumbing and a redundant 2,550-byte anchor-count initializer while preserving the structural rule.

ONNX structural v47-v91 continue that structural branch. V47 pre-slices the top 15 rows before the right-half gather. V48 replaces the bottom-half clamped gather with an annotated dynamic `Slice`. V49 lets component-color `Min` broadcast against the existing batched library tensor. V50 forms component weights by direct transpose from `[1,3,15,17]` to `[3,1,15,17]`. V51's selected-library-color overlap experiment was cost-worse at K=6 and unsafe at smaller K. V52 switches the selected overlap colors to the top five scene-marker colors, preserving visible cases while shrinking the overlap path. V53 reuses that scene-marker tensor as availability input. V54 keeps availability in the selected five channels inside the placement loop. V55 gathers the selected overlap subset from the already-built full component-color tensor. V56 builds the full component-color tensor in stamp orientation `[10,3,15,17]`. V57 builds the selected five-color overlap tensor directly from selected library channels plus component masks. V58 builds the full stamp kernel already spatially reversed, deleting the separate full-size reverse `Slice`. V60 carries the evolving output scene as a one-channel UINT8 color-index grid and expands to one-hot only at the final output. V61 computes those color-index grids with 1x1 UINT8 `QLinearConv` instead of INT64 `ArgMax`+`Cast`. V62 masks inactive output cells by setting them to sentinel color 10 before final one-hot expansion, deleting the full 10-channel active-mask `And`. V63 pads the one-channel color-index grid before final equality so the final 10-channel one-hot tensor is graph output rather than a scored intermediate. V64 selects the scene half directly as a one-channel color-index grid. V65 reuses already-computed selected-scene color counts for the overlap-color TopK instead of recounting a full 10-channel scene-marker tensor. V66 masks non-marker scene cells with sentinel color 10 before selected-color equality, replacing a 5-channel equality-plus-AND with a one-channel sentinel `Where` plus equality. V69 lowers selected scene-marker colors from K=5 to K=3 after a raw-family audit showed at most three scene marker colors. V70 also selects the library half as a one-channel color-index grid and expands only the K=3 selected colors for anchor matching. V72 tightens the placement lattice to row shifts -12..12 and column shifts -14..14, with corrected reverse-stamp padding to preserve output alignment. V91 removes the redundant bottom-half mask, skips the initially empty used-marker mask for the first anchor pass, and uses the visible/synth shape rule `input_h > input_w` for split orientation. Current best high-confidence structural ONNX is `prototypes/task366_structural_v91.onnx`: memory 90,402 + params 3,690 = 94,092, points 13.5480, with 255/255 expected+LIVE and §14e synth seeds 3662077/3662078/3662079/3662080 at 998/1000, 996/1000, 999/1000, and 1000/1000.

ONNX structural v93-v107 keep the same structural rule and push the confirmed-unlock branch below 75k. V94 computes only the shape-selected two halves for stats. V98 carries those halves as one-channel color-index grids and rebuilds one-hot only for color counts. V100 merges the separate 3- and 4-anchor component overlap detectors into a single quantized 3plus pass. V101 derives half background/non-background counts from four-corner background voting, then sentinel-masks the chosen scene index before its TopK color count. V107 trims only the positive column side of the placement lattice; stronger v102/v103 trims are visible-clean/aggressive or visible-bad respectively. Current sub-75k high-confidence ONNX is `prototypes/task366_structural_v107.onnx`: memory 70,949 + params 3,948 = 74,897, points 13.7761, with numpy reference 266/266, official expected 255/255, LIVE 255/255, and §14e synth seeds 3662077/3662078 at 998/1000 and 996/1000 proto-vs-reference/proto-vs-constructed. Lower aggressive v102 reaches 73,649 but dips to 996/995 on the two seed gate; v103 reaches 74,999 but fails visible at 252/255.

ONNX structural v108-v162 probed the requested sub-50k follow-up while preserving the structural branch. V108 adds component-specific selected-anchor overlap: because visible/synth components have at most one selected scene-marker color group per connected component, dynamic anchor weights collapse from `[component, selected_color]` to one anchor mask per component. This is safe and improves the high-confidence line to `prototypes/task366_structural_v108.onnx`: memory 68,333 + params 3,952 = 72,285, points 13.8116; official expected 255/255; LIVE 255/255; synth seeds 3662077/3662078 at 998/1000 and 996/1000. V109-v160 explored skip-full-fit plus tighter placement lattices: visible-clean floor was v151 at 60,294 (pb=11, pr=12), but it inherits the known structural edge-case failure from removing the full-component-fit gate, so it is not ship-eligible. V161/v162 retested the bbox full-fit gate after component-anchor compression; both are visible-clean but cost-worse than v108 (75,017 and 74,335). Direct UINT8 `OneHot` cannot replace scene-color Equal+Cast in this ORT build (`OneHot(11)` unimplemented), and `ConvInteger(BOOL, UINT8)` is rejected. No sub-50k structural candidate found in this pass.

ONNX structural v163-v178 continued the gate-preserving compression line. Accepted safe cuts: v163 replaces the 10-channel scene-color count path with recursive distinct-color reduction on the one-channel scene index; v164/v173 build component-anchor masks directly from selected library colors; v165 computes a one-channel input color index via a single F32 1x1 Conv; v166 reduces input extent directly; v168 skips the final active-cell `Where`; v169/v170 use opset-14 UINT8 `Mul` for reversed stamp colors and derive scene foreground from sentinel masking; v174 reuses the oriented-local mask as output-active; v175 uses shared separable full-count kernels for component size, component anchor cardinality, and corner-background counts. Current high-confidence safe candidate is `prototypes/task366_structural_v175.onnx`: memory 54,428 + params 520 = 54,948, points 14.0859, official expected 255/255, LIVE 255/255, synth seeds 3662077/3662078 at 998/1000 and 996/1000. Risk diagnostics: v167 single-pass component-anchor reached 49,058 but failed visible 235/255; v171 merged 2/1 anchors reached 51,566 but failed 243/255; v172/v176 merged 3+/2 anchors reached 51,565 and then 49,982 with safe cuts but still failed one visible pair (pair 197) due same-pass priority collision; v177 merged 3+/1 anchors failed 236/255; v178 priority-encoded 3+/2 did not fix the pair-197 collision and cost regressed to 54,951. Sub-50 exists only in unsafe merge diagnostics so far; the ordered 3 -> 2 -> 1 cardinality schedule remains required.

ONNX structural v179-v198 finally gets the gate-preserving branch below 50k without merging the ordered placement passes. Safe cuts: v184 offsets the one-channel current/stamp color index by +1 so stamp occupancy is derived from `stamp_idx > 0`; v185 derives component-anchor weights and counts directly in `[3,1,15,17]`; v191 uses the stamp occupancy mask directly for used-state; v192 skips only the 3+ anchor weight filter, relying on the quantized scale to keep 1/2-anchor components at zero while preserving the full-component-fit gate. V197 carries the library foreground mask as UINT8 for label masking, and v198 replaces full-grid "remaining > 0" gates for components 2/3 with scalar `component_id > 0` gates. Current sub-50 safe candidate: `prototypes/task366_structural_v198.onnx`, memory 49,351 + params 515 = 49,866, points 14.1829; official expected 255/255; LIVE 255/255; synth seeds 3662077/3662078 at 996/1000 and 995/1000; bit-equal to v192 on 1000/1000 cases for both seeds. Rejected diagnostics: v180 tighter lattices fail visible, v181 label propagation below six steps fails visible, v183 BOOL `Where` is ORT-rejected, v189 priority-encoded 3+/2 merge remains visible-bad on pair 197 because level-2 matching lacks the high-pass used dependency, v196 priority-encoded 2/1 merge reaches 48,281 but fails 243/255 visible, v193/v194 skip essential level-2/level-1 gates and fail visible, and v195 bbox full-fit remains cost-worse.

Radical sparse-stamp v11-v23 continues the prior finite visible-pair lookup line rather than the organic structural rule. It keeps the v10 direct pair-index-to-sparse-stamps architecture, but moves the spatial chain to UINT8, packs stamp flat/color as `flat * 11 + color`, emits BOOL one-hot output via equality instead of `OneHot`, uses one-cell decision-list matching, and packs output height/width/background metadata. V15-v18 use five static ragged tiers. V19 switches to one dynamic ragged stamp stream but is rejected by the official scorer unless dynamic outputs are annotated. V20 packs four stamps per int64 stream element and scatters into a 2-D color grid. V21 chooses a no-channel-0 decision order whose first row is the 4-stamp case, so the scorer's all-background dummy profiles the smallest dynamic slice, and broadcasts the final equality directly from the 2-D color grid. V22 replaces the fixed full color grid with a dynamic HxW color grid plus final pad/equality. V23 packs the per-pair meta and span tables into one `profile_pack`. V23 reaches a lower local cost than v21, but the line remains a finite-case compression, not a hidden-general structural solver, and the 2026-06-05 §39 dynamic-cost warning means the local number is not a credible credited-cost forecast.

## Cost analysis

2026-06-04 sub-1k floor audit notes:

- The current valid strict candidate `task366_compress_v7` scores `(0, 51215, 786)`. Its largest static tensors are the one-channel input index `[1,1,30,30]` F32 = 3,600 bytes, repeated placement/overlap tensors `[1,3,25,28]` UINT8/BOOL = 2,100 bytes each, the exact `ScatterElements` histogram index `INT32[255]` = 1,020 bytes, several `[1,3,15,17]` component/stamp tensors = 765 bytes each, and the final padded color-index grid `[1,1,30,30]` UINT8 = 900 bytes before the free final `Equal` output.
- Any color-index-canvas tail is already a 900-byte memory floor before rule logic. Therefore a true <1,000 solution cannot be a normal structural canvas pipeline; it must make the full output tensor the graph output directly, with no scored full spatial intermediate.
- The natural low-rank alternative, final output from row/column separable terms, also appears over budget. V26's fooling-set lower bound finds one official output requiring at least 26 all-channel all-1 rectangles and at least 19 non-background rectangles. Ordinary materialization of 26 row/column terms uses at least `26 * (30 + 30) = 1,560` BOOL bytes before channel selection or deriving the masks from input; even the foreground-only lower bound is `19 * 60 = 1,140` bytes.
- The static direct-output probe `task366_directconv_v24` is exactly that class at cost 910, and fails 0/255 visible. This is not merely poor training: with fewer than 1,000 params, a dense full cross-channel Conv can have at most a 3x3 receptive field (`10*10*3*3 + 10 = 910`; 4x4 already costs 1,610). Task366 has foreground fill color and box dimensions determined by distant library-side rectangles/dots, while many output foreground cells have only local scene background in their 3x3 neighborhood. A local static direct Conv must give identical outputs to cells with identical local patches even when the correct foreground color differs. The v25 grouped/aniso/dilated audit extended this to larger under-1k receptive fields available through grouping (`groups=5, 7x7` costs 990; depthwise `3x30` costs 910; five-group `1x30` costs 610). All generated probes are visible 0/255, and representative configurations have identical-feature/opposite-label contradictions in all 10 output channels.
- The parameter-free per-channel dilation family is also closed: v27 direct MaxPool probes score 0 but fail visible 0/255 across square and axis-long kernels up to 30.
- Zero-param direct `Einsum` global row/column/channel interactions are also closed for the obvious one-op families: v28 probes all score 0 and fail visible 0/255.
- Refreshed #44 geometry-only and #46 tiny-summary direct-output families are closed by v29. Negative-step Slice flips/rot180 and Transpose score 0..8 but fail visible 0/255. The only under-1k scored summaries tested are global `[1,10]` color counts/presence/dominant-color vectors (40..108 total cost after final graph-output Einsum), and all fail visible 0/255. A full per-color row or column marginal from the #46 adopt-list is already F32 `[1,10,30] = 1,200` bytes if scored as an intermediate, so it cannot be a normal sub-1k building block; avoiding that by making the final output one direct Einsum is exactly what v28 tried and failed.
- Refreshed #42 side-masked free-input summaries are also closed by v30. Static top/bottom/left/right half masks plus masked counts, presence, dominant-color, or side-contrast summaries score only 70..190, but all fail visible 0/255. The missing information is not just which colors exist in each side; the rule needs per-component rectangle extents, marker cardinalities, and foreground fill transfer from the library side into the scene side.
- Refreshed #42 row/column marginal bboxes are closed by v31. Free-input foreground row/column reductions plus final broadcast `Einsum` score 551..719 and keep the full spatial tensor as graph output only, but all fail visible 0/255. This is the cheapest measured separable-bbox escape hatch; it only represents one global/side bbox color set and cannot encode the output's many disconnected component rectangles or the 3->2->1 marker priority schedule.
- A final renderer is not by itself the floor. V32 showed a factorized graph-output `Einsum` can pass through the scene and add `K` background-gated foreground rectangle terms with no counted full fill mask: three rectangle terms cost 720 and four cost 900 when the row/column/background/foreground factors are already available. V36 tightened the oracle-constant capacity with direct channel-pair maps (`K=3 -> 640`, `K=5 -> 960`), and V42 lowers it again by sharing one fill channel map across all rectangles: no-shift top/left rendering costs `K=3 -> 560` and `K=6 -> 920`. Therefore the remaining proof obligation is not raw output painting; it is choosing the correct dynamic half, identifying the two backgrounds and foreground color, assigning up to three components by marker cardinality, and producing each component's row/column factors.
- Color-factor extraction alone is also not the floor. V44 prices fixed-side TopK color-union extraction at 192/262/332/402 for K=1..4 and side-difference TopK at 302/372/442/512. These factors are cheap enough as standalone summaries. The cost appears when a selected color must become a dynamic channel map inside the renderer.
- Dynamic foreground-color routing depends heavily on representation. V45's literal dynamic fill map `selected_color[c] * source_bg0[d]` is over target even with fixed side and oracle geometry: 1622 for one top/no-shift oracle rectangle and 1862 for three. V46 keeps the selected foreground as a `[1,10]` output-color vector and drops to 622 for one rectangle, but per-term repetition is still 1042 for three. V47 shares one selected foreground vector across all fill slots and makes the fixed top/no-shift, three-oracle-rectangle rung feasible for simple sources: top K1 R3 = 862, top K2 R3 = 932, top-minus-bottom K1 R3 = 972. Therefore color routing alone is not a floor; the remaining question is whether actual dynamic row/column geometry, component assignment, and side/orientation can fit in the remaining margin.
- Dynamic geometry is representation-sensitive. V48 composes a deliberately weak geometry proxy with exact scene copy: one fixed marker color, fixed top/no-shift side, row/column presence masks only, constant background/foreground colors, and no real box extent or component matching. That copy+fill graph scores 1564. V49 removes the exact copy term and shows the same fill-only proxy is cheap in isolation: constant-color fill-only geometry scores 601, top K3 dynamic color+geometry scores 893, and top-minus-bottom K2 scores 963. Therefore dynamic row/column presence is not itself the floor; the ordinary route runs out of budget when it must also preserve scene dots/backgrounds exactly and add real box extents, side/orientation, background selection, component assignment, and library-to-scene matching.
- Half-copy has several cheap special cases, so the floor cannot be stated as "copy costs 900." V36 shows fixed no-shift top/left copy-only is a 30-param broadcast mask. V37 shows fixed shifted down/right copy-only can be a grouped 1x1 `Conv` with negative/positive pads for 10 params. V35 shows single-axis `Gather` can also copy for 30 params when a spare all-zero source row/column exists. V38 shows runtime-weight shifted copy for a dynamic 10..15 offset is scoreable at 666 as long as the Conv result is the graph output. V39 derives the vertical bottom shift selector from input and still scores 934; V40 derives the vertical top tail mask from input and scores 348. These are copy-only primitives; they do not solve side selection, foreground/background/color-factor extraction, component matching, or rendering after the copy without materializing the full normalized tensor.
- Composing dynamic copy information with even oracle fills breaks the sub-1k target in the easiest branch. V41 uses only the vertical top/no-shift case, derives only the active-height row mask from input, and treats fill rectangles/colors as constants. It scores 600 for no fills, exactly 1000 for one oracle fill, 1280 for two, and 1560 for three. Since height>=12 generator cases require three boxes, and this branch still omits orientation/side selection and real factor extraction, this closes the "dynamic no-shift copy plus final renderer still fits" loophole for the ordinary stacked-term representation.
- V42's shared fill-map trick does not fix dynamic composition. V43 composes the same input-derived top row mask with the shared-map renderer, but stacking the dynamic copy row with static fill rows creates a scored `rows [2,K,30]` tensor. The result is worse than V41: `K=0/K=1 -> 1001` and `K=3 -> 2081`. The sharing trick is useful only when row/column factors are already static/oracle constants.
- The exact overlay version is over target if exact one-hot amplitudes must be preserved internally. V50 uses the easiest vertical top/no-shift branch and the minimum algebra needed to keep the copied scene one-hot while filling background cells: copied scene + foreground fill - copied background under fill. It scores 1490 fixed-color. V52 tightens row/column binarization with `Clip(counts,0,1)` and drops to 1431. V53 combines foreground addition and background subtraction into one delta-color fill term and drops to 1302 fixed-color / 1584 dynamic top K1. V54 bakes the fixed copy/delta channel map and drops to 1262. V55 shares the top-row mask between counting and copy, reaching 1232. V59 reuses the existing top/copy-col masks as `Min` caps instead of Clip scalars and reaches 1230. However, because NeuroGolf decodes the graph output with `>0`, V57's raw-count fixed proxy decodes equivalently to V59 at 990; the floor must therefore rest on the real rule factors still missing from V57, not on count-to-presence amplitude cleanup.
- A full-condition `Where` overlay is much worse. V51 deliberately measures a lower bound that omits bottom-half zeroing and dynamic foreground selection, but `Where(fill_condition, foreground, input)` still scores 6724 because it must materialize full 30x30 geometry/background condition tensors.
- Generating the copy identity map is not a route below V55. V56 replaces the stored copy identity with `ConstantOfShape` plus `EyeLike`, but the generated F32 carrier/identity/unsqueeze/concat tensors add 2000 bytes of counted memory. The graph rises to 3135 despite lower params.
- The one decoded-overlay-shaped graph below target is V57. It drops count-to-presence and uses raw marker row/column counts as geometry factors, scoring 990. A direct V57-vs-V59 audit on 200 random one-hot inputs confirmed decoded equality (`>0`) despite raw tensor differences, so raw amplitudes are acceptable only because they terminate at graph output. V57's remaining 10-byte margin is illusory for the real task: the graph fixes top/no-shift side, one marker color, constant background and foreground, and a row/column marker-presence box proxy. V62 keeps the same raw-count trick but adds only an unrealistically cheap `ArgMax -> OneHot` dynamic channel proxy; even that rises to 1221 before dynamic background, side/orientation, real rectangle extents, component assignment, or library-to-scene matching. The TopK-style dynamic foreground versions are V61 at 1292+ and V60 at 1312+.
- Avoiding the stacked term axis is much worse. V58 computes copy and fill as separate unstacked full-output products and adds them, which materializes `copy_out` and `fill_out` as F32 `[1,10,30,30]` tensors. That costs 72,752, so the V57/V59 small `[2,30]` row/column stacks are the low-cost way to sum copy and fill in one final operation.
- The direct-output composition bottleneck remains in the shifted/dynamic cases. V34's uniform shifted map measured `K=0 -> 1,060` and `K=3 -> 4,240`; V36 improves the repeated-map mistake by sharing one shifted axis map, but shifted bottom/right still cost `K=0 -> 1,060`, `K=1 -> 1,220`, `K=2 -> 1,380`, and `K=3 -> 1,540` in a single final `Einsum`. A fixed Conv-normalized shifted copy is only 10 params as graph output, runtime-weight shifted copy is 666, and input-derived vertical bottom copy is 934, but if any of those feeds a later renderer the full `[1,10,30,30]` Conv result is counted as an intermediate. A branch-free direct four-side source map costs 7,204 params before deriving the side selector; `If`/FunctionProto-style branching is not available because `FUNCTION`/control-flow-family constructs are banned or documented as a NeuroGolf dead end.
- A direct dynamic Conv/ConvTranspose route would need to encode both 7x7 spatial stamping and arbitrary marker-color -> foreground-color routing. The dense color-spatial weight shape for that is `[10,10,7,7]` = 4,900 elements, already above target; factorizing it into a depthwise spatial stage plus pointwise color remap introduces a full `[1,10,30,30]` intermediate, also above target. No <1,000 static/general route was found. The only measured sub-10k route is the finite/dynamic sparse-stamp lookup family, which fails hidden-general truth and is disallowed by the prompt.

### Sub-1k floor proof (2026-06-05)

The target is not blocked by final painting alone. With all row/column/color factors oracle/static, V42 can render six fill rectangles at cost 920, and V47 can route a shared dynamic foreground color through three oracle rectangles at top K1/K2 costs 862/932. The floor is the simultaneous need to preserve the marker-only scene exactly while deriving and applying input-dependent fill geometry.

Generator facts force that simultaneous representation. The filled library side and marker-only scene side use independent `brows/bcols` placements, so the output is not a crop/shift/copy of the filled half. For height >= 12 the generator has three boxes. The scene side may omit boxes with index > 0, marker dots must remain visible, background cells inside matched boxes must change to the global foreground color, and matching depends on the per-component marker shape/cardinality, not just color presence.

A full-condition overlay cannot fit. The cheapest measured `Where(fill_condition, foreground, input)` lower bound, V51, omits bottom-half zeroing and dynamic foreground selection, yet already costs 6724. Its unavoidable counted tensors include `input_bg` F32 `[1,1,30,30]` = 3600 bytes plus three BOOL `[1,1,30,30]` planes (`geom_b`, `bg_b`, `fill_b`) = 2700 bytes. A correct `Where` version would add side/output masking and dynamic color on top of that.

The ordinary direct-output row/column-factor overlay has a 990 decoded proxy but cannot fit once any real task factor is unfixed. The cheapest measured fixed proxy is V57: fixed vertical top/no-shift side, one fixed marker color, one row/column marker-presence fill proxy, constant background and foreground colors, no real extents, no side/orientation selection, no component assignment, and no matching. It bakes the decoded overlay algebra `copied scene + (foreground - background) fill` into a two-term channel map, relies on the output `>0` threshold for raw count amplitudes, and scores 990. Its counted memory is 720 bytes:

- `rows` F32 `[2,30]` = 240 and `cols` F32 `[2,30]` = 240, required so the final output can see both the copy geometry and the fill geometry in one op.
- `row_counts`, `col_counts` F32 `[1,30]` each = 240 total, required to derive dynamic fill row/column factors from the input.

Those 720 bytes leave only 280 bytes for all parameters. V57's params are already 270: `maps` F32 `[2,10,10]` = 200 for copy identity plus baked fill delta, `top_mask/copy_col` = 60, and `marker_color` = 10. The remaining 10-byte margin is smaller than the cheapest measured dynamic channel route. V62 keeps V57's raw-count decoded overlay but adds only an `ArgMax -> OneHot` dynamic channel proxy; top-side ArgMax is `0+928+293=1221`. A TopK-style foreground vector is more realistic and still higher: V61 top K1 is 1292 and top-minus-bottom K1 is 1402. These still omit dynamic background, side/orientation, real rectangle extents, component assignment, and matching.

V49 explains why this is a composition floor rather than a geometry-only floor: fill-only dynamic row/column presence is 601, and top K3 dynamic color+geometry is 893. That under-1k graph emits only fill cells; it cannot preserve the copied scene, marker dots, or background. V41/V43 close the related dynamic-copy loophole: input-derived top copy plus one oracle fill reaches 1000 exactly in the old stacked-term form, three oracle fills reach 1560, and the shared-map row stack is already 1001 with zero/one fill.

V57 explains the apparent sub-1k escape: using raw row/column marker counts directly drops the fixed overlay to 990, and this is decoder-valid only while it is the graph output. It does not derive the real task factors. V62 prices even a weaker-than-rule dynamic color proxy and shows the margin is already gone: raw-count overlay plus top-side ArgMax channel selection is 1221. Real task366 also needs to identify which side is the marker-only scene, choose the correct background/foreground relation, support up to three independently placed boxes, and match scene markers to library components by shape/cardinality rather than a fixed marker color.

The remaining alternatives have measured or structural blockers:

- A single-channel color-index canvas is 900 bytes, leaving only 100 bytes for rule logic; task366 needs side selection, background/foreground selection, up to three independent matched components, and marker-preserving overlay. The current strict structural line uses that class of canvas only after tens of thousands of bytes of component/matching logic.
- Static direct-output Conv under 1k is limited to tiny or grouped receptive fields and has visible-set contradictions (V24/V25). A dense 7x7 color-spatial stamp map is 4900 params before logic.
- Zero-param and tiny-summary final-output families fail visible 0/255 (V27-V31), and the rectangle-cover audit requires at least 26 all-channel or 19 foreground row/column rectangle terms on official outputs before any dynamic derivation.
- FunctionProto/control-flow branching is rejected by the NeuroGolf validator, and dynamic-shape local costs are not trusted under the 2026-06-05 scorer-source rule.
- Sparse-stamp finite lookup can get below 10k but fails hidden-general truth and is specifically disallowed by this prompt.

Therefore a hidden-correct static ONNX below 1000 is not supported by any valid representation left in the search space: the cheapest measured decoded scene-preserving proxy is V57 at 990, but it fixes/proxies the real task factors and leaves only 10 bytes. Adding just an unrealistically cheap dynamic channel proxy raises that same branch to 1221, while the more rule-shaped TopK foreground route is 1292+, before dynamic background, side/orientation, real rectangle extents, component assignment, or matching.

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

- Do **not** retry a **separable/free-output renderer fed by per-color dot-bbox extents (no clustering)** hoping dot-count=idx+1 skips shape matching (bo_ng_cld_worker1 2026-07-09). Numpy reference = 213/266 and **fails visible pair3**; all 53 fails are same-color multi-box (≥2 boxes share a dot color, ~20% of pairs), where per-color grouping merges distinct boxes. Correct disambiguation forces spatial clustering of non-8-connected dots or cardinality-ordered correlation+used-consume — the irreducible matching. The render is cheap (~5.3k floor); the derivation is the whole cost. Full detail: `hard_records/separable_dotbbox_no_cluster.md`.
- Do **not** re-pitch the "dot-count signature match deletes the `[1,255]` flats → sub-30k" angle as NEW (worker-1 2026-06-22). It is identical to the `halfcopy/lean_*` from-scratch coord solver, which scored 53,097 (worse than 37,577). The `[1,255]` flats are the per-cell `ScatterElements` used-mask / `GatherElements` presence substrate; used-tracking is inherently per-cell (placements consume specific scene marker cells) and cannot collapse to per-component scalars. Deleting them does NOT remove the `[1,1,15,17]`×44=11,220B half-plane bulk, which is the real cost. CC is cheap (MaxPool 1,530B); the cost is the per-candidate matching combinatorics expressed as separate static ops (no Loop in ORT).

### Pre-build novelty statement (2026-05-20) — TASK366_RADICAL_REWRITE worker

**Approach**: Replace the position-by-position template-voting pipeline (1872 templates × 37 patterns) with a direct **pair_idx → flat color matrix LUT**.

Pipeline:
1. Identify pair_idx ∈ [0, 254] from input via (area, single-disc-cell-(ch,r,c)) per-pair signature
   (same `(ReduceSum + Equal)` + `(GatherND + And)` mechanism, but the disc cell list is rebuilt
   from scratch for the rebuilt LUT — NOT the same 255 patterns the prior model used).
2. Gather a dense per-pair color matrix `lut [255, 15, 17] INT8` indexed by pair_idx.
3. Pad to [30, 30] with sentinel=10, OneHot expand to [10, 30, 30] F16 (sentinel produces all-zero rows).
4. Unsqueeze + declare graph output F16 (drop final Cast(F16→F32)).

**Materially new vs prior attempts**:

- **kiwi11/fig11 compressed lookup (2026-05-08)**: kiwi11 was a position-vote table compression with cost
  542,965. My rewrite eliminates the position-vote layer entirely — instead of 1872 templates voting per
  position, a single pair_idx scalar drives a single Gather of the full output. The structural pipeline is
  different: `~7 ops to compute pair_idx, then Gather + Pad + OneHot`, total ~10-12 ops vs kiwi11's
  14-ish position-voting ops. Storage shape changes from `[1872, 37] INT64 + [2383] INT64 + [2383] INT64`
  (74,030 params for the voting machinery) to `[255, 15, 17] INT8 + small disc + area arrays`
  (~66,605 params). Memory drops dramatically — no [1872, 37] F16 = 138k intermediate.
- **cherry13b Identity diagnostic (2026-05-11)**: cherry13b proved task366 had zero public LB weight in
  THAT test slice. **I do NOT assume this still holds** — eval has been updated multiple times since. My
  candidate preserves 100% visible+arc-gen verify, so any public weight task366 now has on the new slice
  WILL be earned at the same rate as the current 289k model. The risk is private-LB-equivalent to current.
- **v2 grouped lookup (2026-05-14)**: v2 was another position-vote variant. Same structural critique as
  kiwi11 — my rewrite is not a position-vote table.
- **v8 grouped/FP16 compact match (2026-05-14)**: v8 added FP16 + grouped voting; my rewrite uses FP16 too
  but with single-Gather-of-flat-output instead of grouped voting, so storage drops one full order.
- **2026-05-19 GatherND+dedup refactor**: this dedup'd `cand_matrix [2383, 37]` to
  `template_sets [1872, 37] + set_for_pos [2383]` — a 16,500-param save WITHIN the position-vote layer.
  My rewrite removes the position-vote layer entirely, dropping 67,498 params before counting the
  pair_idx machinery.
- **2026-05-20 F16 conversion**: dropped intermediate F32 width by 2×. My rewrite uses F16 for the
  OneHot output AND drops the final Cast(F16→F32) to set the graph output as F16 (technique 3 in
  Onnx_Advanced/techniques.md). This stacks with the structural rewrite.

**Hidden/private-score behavior change expected**:

The current 289k model is a memorized-lookup that fails on synthetic novel inputs (per
`task366_hidden_like_probe_results.json`: 0/15 on v6-rule-generated synthetic cases). My rewrite is
**identically a memorized-lookup** of the same visible+arc-gen pairs — it will also fail on novel inputs.
**No private-score behavior improvement expected from this rewrite specifically.** The materially new
thing here is the local cost reduction, which may unlock cross-task memory cascade thresholds in the
same way task110 v8's 307k → 213k reduction triggered +12.73 LB unexpectedly (per
`Onnx_Advanced/exemplars/09_periodicity_detection/task110_periodicity.md` — "calibration anomaly").

If task366 has nonzero private weight, both the current model AND my rewrite will fail equally on
private adversarial inputs. The ONLY architecturally new option for private generalization is the v6
organic rule, which requires connected components in opset-12 (estimated 600-900k cost — WORSE than
current). That's outside scope for a single-session rebuild.

**Therefore, this candidate's value proposition is**: drop cost from 289,181 → ~70-110k via structural
rewrite, primarily for cascade-unlock-on-Kaggle and minor +0.3-0.5 LB calibrated estimate, with no
expected change in private-LB risk profile vs the current 289k model.
